page: Amazon Web Services r6id.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The server configuration delivers 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores using hyperthreading on the x86_64 architecture, supported by 54 MB of Level 3 cache. System memory totals 1024 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Integrated hardware includes 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps. The instance does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reflects strong parallel compute and high memory throughput capabilities. In multi-threaded CPU stress testing, the instance scored 123840.21 on stress-ng and 87085.72 on the PassMark CPU suite, ranking in the upper tiers. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 334.55 GB/sec, accompanied by 135.74 GB/sec in uncached write throughput. Application-level metrics demonstrate 106.91 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, alongside strong database operation test scores. Conversely, single-threaded execution metrics remain within median industry ranges, indicating that aggregate parallel capacity outpaces individual core execution.

The inclusion of 7.6 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage delivers high I/O throughput without remote network storage overhead, though instance store data remains ephemeral. This dense memory and local storage profile presents strong resource efficiency for data platforms requiring rapid caching tiers or massive scratch space. The r6id.32xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, distributed data processing, relational database management systems, and compilation jobs.
